title: segment_to_map_report
description: One-time run of the map-segments pipeline against the single shared segment_id_mapping/segment_to_map.json export (5315 rows), which interleaves pi-1 Pali, pi-1's English translation, pi-2 Pali, and a partial pi-2 English translation. Each of the four combinations below was matched separately against its own source markdown and its own *_segments.json id registry.
methodology_note: The vault's canonical segment_id_mapping/skill/scripts/map_segments.py was run first (unmodified) and produced a materially incomplete result for pi-1: its unbounded forward exact-match scan plus its fuzzy fallback can jump far ahead onto a coincidental match when the same short formulaic paragraph recurs verbatim at many different references (very common in this Abhidhamma text), permanently stranding legitimate exact matches that sat between the old and new pointer position. For this run only, a throwaway alternative aligner (not saved into the vault / skill/scripts, per instruction) was used instead: a strict order-preserving two-pointer walk with a capped forward window (so it cannot runaway-jump), a safe unique-exact backfill pass for rows left behind by the window cap, and -- only for pi-1, where full coverage was requested -- a small number of manually-verified overrides for source paragraphs the to-map export had split across many non-adjacent rows (e.g. one 41-line rūpasaṅgaho enumeration). Every override was verified by exact string reconstruction (the concatenation of the assigned to-map rows equals the source paragraph's text character-for-character), never by similarity/guessing.
